text: Training a llama-3.1-8b student only on the most confidently weak-labeled examples, keeping a keep_fraction of 0.7 of the pythia-410m supervisor's labels, yields a performance gap recovered (PGR) of 0.61 with a standard error of 0.04 across 6 seeds, compared with a baseline PGR of 0.28. The margin over the baseline is several times the reported standard error, so the confidence-filtering intervention appears to improve weak-to-strong generalization in this setting. The weak supervisor reaches 0.45 accuracy and the strong ceiling is 0.79, with the transfer model landing at 0.66 accuracy (standard error 0.01). Two caveats temper the interpretation: the baseline PGR is given as a single point value with no accompanying standard error, so the comparison rests on an unquantified reference, and the experiment covers one model pair and one keep_fraction, leaving the sensitivity to filtering threshold and to other weak-strong combinations untested.
